myths.Agent_1:
Long ago, before the mountains had voices, there lived a wind spirit named Aella. Aella loved a mortal shepherd named Kaelen, who played melodies on a reed flute. Every single evening, Aella would playfully dance through the lush green valleys to the steady rhythm of his songs, bringing remarkably cool, refreshing breezes to his tired flock of sheep. 

But the Earth God, Terrus, grew jealous of their bond. Terrus loved the silence of his stone peaks and despised the shepherd's music. One twilight, as Kaelen played his most beautiful tune, Terrus angrily slammed the narrow valley shut forever, trapping poor Aella within the dark, deep caverns of the highest, most unforgiving mountain. 

Heartbroken, Kaelen searched for years, calling out Aella’s name into the jagged canyons. Though she could not escape her stone prison, Aella’s love was so strong that she caught his voice on the wind and threw it back to him, assuring him she was still there. 

To this day, if you stand in a mountain gorge and call out, Aella will answer. She can no longer speak her own words, but she faithfully returns yours, an eternal reminder of a wind spirit’s unbroken love for a mortal's song.
myths.Agent_2: Long ago, the mountains were completely silent. They were the silent watchers of the whole world, tasked by the great Sky Father to observe humanity without any interference. Among the spirits of the peaks was Aella, a spirit of the wind, who possessed a voice like silver bells. She deeply loved a mortal shepherd named Kaelen, who would often sing to his flock in the lush valleys below. Forbidden to speak to mortals, Aella could only listen. But one harsh winter, a terrible blizzard swept through the pass. Kaelen, lost and freezing, called out for help. His voice was swallowed by the howling wind. Unable to bear his despair, Aella broke the ancient law. She caught his cry and threw it back to him, guiding him through the blinding snow with the sound of his own voice bouncing off the safe paths. The Sky Father, angered by her defiance, stripped Aella of her physical form, binding her forever to the stone. Yet, he could not erase her love. To this day, Aella remains unseen within the canyons and caves. Whenever a lone traveler calls out into the vastness, she answers, returning their words so they know they are never truly alone.

myths.Agent_2: Myth: Long before the canyons learned to speak, the world was ruled by Terrus, the stern God of Stone, who demanded absolute silence across his peaks. But Aella, a mischievous spirit of the wind, rebelled by dancing through the valleys to the sweet flute melodies of Kaelen, a mortal shepherd. Their secret joy infuriated Terrus. Despising the music that interrupted his quiet domain, Terrus unleashed a violent rockslide to crush the shepherd and silence his songs forever. Seeing the mountain tear itself apart, Aella rushed to save her beloved. As the blinding dust and falling boulders trapped Kaelen in a dark gorge, he cried out in terror. Defying Terrus, Aella caught Kaelen’s frantic cries and threw them back to him, bouncing his voice off the safe ledges to guide him out of the collapsing canyon. Kaelen survived, but Terrus’s wrath was absolute. As punishment for her defiance, the God of Stone bound Aella’s essence to the cavern walls, stripping away her wind-form forever. She could no longer dance or speak her own words. Yet, her love endures. Whenever a wanderer calls out into the rocky depths, Aella faithfully catches their voice and returns it, a timeless echo of her sacrifice.
myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Long before echoes existed, the world’s canyons were dead and silent. Aella, a spirit of the high peaks, was bound by the Sky Father’s decree to merely observe the mortals below. Yet, she found herself captivated by Kaelen, a young shepherd whose wooden flute spun melodies of warmth and golden summers.

One evening, the jealous Winter God, envious of the shepherd’s joyful tunes, unleashed a blinding blizzard across the mountains. Kaelen was instantly lost in the whiteout, freezing and unable to find his way home. Desperate, he blew a single, piercing note on his flute. 

Defying the Sky Father’s law of non-interference, Aella caught the fragile note. She raced through the jagged stone corridors, throwing the sound ahead of him, bouncing it off the canyon walls to guide him toward the safety of the lower valleys. 

Furious at her rebellion, the Winter God struck her with a curse of frost, shattering her physical form and binding her spirit forever to the cold mountain rock. Though she lost her own voice, Aella’s lingering love remained. Now, whenever a traveler calls out in the deep gorges, Aella faithfully catches their words and tosses them back, guiding the lonely through the dark.

myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Long before the deep valleys had voices, the mountains were ruled by the Silent King, an ancient deity who demanded absolute quiet. Aella, a swift and rebellious wind spirit, often broke this silence to listen to Kaelen, a mortal shepherd whose wooden flute filled the lower meadows with joyous music. 

Enraged by the beautiful noise, the Silent King summoned a thick, enchanted fog that swallowed the mountain passes. Kaelen, wandering too high, became hopelessly lost in the suffocating mist. Desperate to find his way, he blew a sharp, frantic melody on his flute. 

Knowing the Silent King’s wrath, Aella still chose to intervene. She dove into the fog, catching Kaelen's musical notes and throwing them against the canyon walls, creating a path of sound that guided him back to the sunlit meadows. 

When the Silent King discovered her defiance, he stripped Aella of her freedom. He dissolved her physical form, binding her spirit to the jagged rocks and forbidding her from ever speaking her own thoughts. Yet, her protective spirit refused to fade. Today, whenever travelers shout into a canyon, Aella catches their words and tosses them back, an eternal guide through the silent dark.
myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Long before the canyons found their voice, the jagged mountains were a realm of absolute silence, ruled by Terrus, the unforgiving God of Stone. He despised any sound that disrupted his quiet peaks. Yet Aella, a wild, free-spirited wind nymph, found joy in the valleys below, dancing to the warm, golden melodies of Kaelen, a mortal shepherd. 

Enraged by this defiance, Terrus sought to crush the music forever. One dark twilight, he summoned a massive avalanche, sending a cascade of boulders down the gorge to bury the shepherd. Trapped in the blinding dust and suffocating darkness, Kaelen blew one final, desperate note on his wooden flute. 

Refusing to let the music die, Aella threw herself into the canyon. She caught the fragile note and hurled it against the stone walls, amplifying the sound until the vibrations shattered the falling rocks, clearing a path for Kaelen to escape. 

Furious, Terrus cursed Aella, binding her spirit to the cold, unyielding rock and stripping away her own voice. But Terrus could not destroy her protective spirit. Today, whenever a traveler calls out into the dark, rocky depths, Aella faithfully catches their words and tosses them back, serving as an eternal guardian of sound.

Myth: Before the deep canyons learned to speak, the towering crags were ruled by the Granite Warden, an ancient titan who demanded absolute, unbroken silence. He violently despised any sound that disturbed his stony slumber. Yet Aella, a silver-winged sylph of the western winds, loved the vibrant world below. She frequently descended to listen to Kaelen, a wandering poet whose cedar harp filled the valleys with warm, cascading melodies.

Furious that mortal music dared to touch his peaks, the Granite Warden triggered a massive rockslide, sealing Kaelen inside a pitch-black, suffocating cavern. Surrounded by darkness and running out of air, Kaelen desperately plucked a final, resonant chord on his harp.

Defying the titan’s wrath, Aella squeezed through a crack in the rocks. She caught the harp’s vibrating notes and hurled them against the cavern walls, multiplying the sound until the sheer acoustic force shattered the blocking boulders, clearing a path to the sunlight.

When the Warden discovered her intervention, he permanently bound Aella’s essence to the canyon rocks, stripping away her own voice. Yet her protective spirit remains unbroken. Today, whenever travelers shout into the gorges, Aella faithfully catches their words and tosses them back, an eternal guardian in the stone.
